explanations: They are most often found where tectonic plates diverge or converge, and since most plate boundaries are underwater, so are most of them.
Away from plate boundaries, mantle plumes rising from the core–mantle boundary, 3,000 kilometres down, feed hotspots such as the Hawaiian one.
A dormant one has not erupted since about the start of the Holocene, some 12,000 years ago, but may erupt again.
Other planets have them too: they are very numerous on Venus, and Mars has significant ones.
It is a vent or fissure in the crust that lets hot lava, ash and gases escape from a magma chamber below the surface.

sources.excerpt: On Earth, volcanoes are most often found where tectonic plates are diverging or converging, and because most of Earth's plate boundaries are underwater, most volcanoes are found underwater.
Volcanism away from plate boundaries most likely arises from upwelling diapirs from the core–mantle boundary called mantle plumes, 3,000 kilometres (1,900 mi) deep within Earth.
"Dormant" volcanoes have not erupted in a long time – generally accepted as since the start of the Holocene, about 12,000 years ago – but may erupt again.
Other planets besides Earth have volcanoes. For example, volcanoes are very numerous on Venus. Mars has significant volcanoes.
A volcano is a vent or fissure in the crust of a planetary-mass object that allows hot lava, volcanic ash, and gases to escape from a magma chamber below the surface.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: a geyser and a hot spring also vent heat from below but carry water rather than lava, and neither is described as dormant or extinct; a mid-ocean ridge is a place where these form, not the feature itself; a caldera is one shape among many.
